payload.objective: Deliver the next serialized concrete provider adapter group after accepted IMP-PROV-03. Move Cursor and OpenCode live execution behind private Providers Execution adapters that implement the accepted Providers root protocol and shared conformance suite. Preserve observable invocation, streaming/final-result, negotiation/fallback where applicable, cancellation, timeout, safe diagnostics, provider-session reference, and failure behavior while deleting only the superseded Cursor/OpenCode legacy branches.
scope: Use pkg/services/providers as the standalone owner and keep concrete implementations parent-private under Execution.
Cursor and OpenCode each load identity/capability metadata from the Providers-owned catalog and register through the accepted execution registry.
Preserve Cursor Windows prompt/stream/session/failure behavior and OpenCode negotiation/fallback/decode/session/failure behavior with observable parity.

Prove canonical request mapping, ordered progress/tool/message drafts, exactly one terminal result, cancellation/timeout normalization, safe diagnostics, and provider-session metadata through shared conformance and focused functional tests entered through root.BuildProcess.
Delete only Cursor/OpenCode aggregate execution, decoding, failure, timeout, and session branches that are actually replaced; do not add a new provider switch or duplicate catalog.

Do not edit top-level CLI/Cobra composition, authored OpenAPI/generation, Packaged Factory catalog ownership, Provider Sessions readers, Models, Automations wire folds, or unrelated providers (Gemini/Kiro/Pi/Agy).
Treat shared coverage, ownership, and package-target manifest churn as accepted integration work; rebase and reconcile it through delivery.
acceptanceCriteria: Cursor and OpenCode execute only through their Providers-owned private adapters and the accepted Providers execution registry.
Each adapter passes the shared provider conformance protocol plus focused public functional tests entered through root.BuildProcess.
Streaming, final selection, tool correlation, negotiation/fallback where applicable, cancellation, timeout, normalized failures, and detached Provider Session references retain observable parity.
No shared orchestration switch gains a Cursor or OpenCode case, and replaced legacy branches are removed in the same slice.
Required focused tests, package-boundary/file-count checks, relevant functional gates, and repository verification pass.
payload.deliveryContract: Continue the implementation and review loop until every required CI check is terminal and passing, every blocking PR conversation comment is addressed, merge conflicts are resolved, and the PR is merged. Only then may Factory work complete. Opening a PR, making it review-ready, or obtaining green CI without merge is not completion. Shared-file churn is not an admission blocker; rebase and reconcile shared files as part of this delivery loop.
payload.requestedOutcome: Implement IMP-PROV-04 by migrating Cursor and OpenCode live execution into parent-private Providers Execution adapters bound through the accepted catalog-backed execution registry. Preserve observable Cursor and OpenCode request, stream, negotiation/fallback, tool/message correlation, final-result, cancellation, timeout, diagnostics, failure, and detached Provider Session reference behavior. Remove only aggregate legacy Cursor/OpenCode branches superseded by the cutover. Do not admit IMP-PROV-05/06, LWR-PROV, Workers fold/DEL, Automations/Recordings/PSES wire folds, OpenAPI fan-in, or PSS-I03. Explicitly loop through implementation and review until required CI is terminal green, every blocking PR conversation comment is addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file churn are reconciled, the PR is merged, and only then complete the Factory work.
